newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tobishima shares bid-only in early morning Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Tobishima shares bid-only in early morning Tokyo.

text.p: Shares in Tobishima Corp were bid-only in early morning Tokyo trade on Wednesday, aided by a newspaper report that creditors of the debt-ridden firm had agreed to accept its restructuring plan, brokers said.
As of 0028 GMT, the shares were bid-only at 219 yen, compared with Tuesday's close of 209 yen.
Other construction shares were also solid in morning trade, with Obayashi Corp up nine yen at 750 yen as of 0058 GMT with turnover of 367,000.
Shimizu Corp shares were also up seven yen at 700 yen, while Kumagai Gumi Co Ltd rose 10 yen to 193 yen, becoming the third largest percentage gainer on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
A Tobishima spokesman told Reuters on Wednesday that many of its creditor financial institutions were moving towards acceptance of its restructuring plan.
But he declined to comment specifically on a report by the Nihon Keizai Shimbun business daily on Wednesday that they had already agreed to accept the firm's restructuring plan.
The newspaper reported the plan includes a sharp reduction in their claims against Tobishima for its group firms' debts.
The restructuring plan, drawn up last year, asks creditors to reduce their claims against the construction firm for its group companies' debt to 100 billion yen from about 740 billion yen.
There are more than 50 creditor financial institutions, of which Fuji Bank Ltd is the main creditor.
